before.title: Active Exhaust Valve Seizure and Cable Rot (VR-4)
before.description: Early VR-4s have an Active Exhaust System with a driver-selectable Tour/Sport valve in the rear exhaust; the system was phased out after the 1994 model year. The valve shaft corrodes and seizes (usually stuck in the quiet Tour position) and the actuator cable rots away, so toggling the switch changes nothing. The valve's D-shaped shaft rounds off so the external lever can move while the internal plate stays shut, and the sealed assembly cannot be easily disassembled for repair.
before.solution: Free a seized valve with extended penetrating-oil soaks and careful heat cycles — a well-documented community procedure — and replace the rotted actuator cable, or fit a replacement/used valve assembly. Many owners simply wire the valve open or delete it with an aftermarket exhaust.
symptoms: No exhaust tone change when switching between Tour and Sport
Exhaust permanently quiet and restrictive (valve stuck in Tour)
Active exhaust switch light works but nothing happens
Corroded or detached actuator cable at the rear muffler valve

before.title: AWD Transfer Case Oil Leak Leading to Bearing Failure and Driveline Lockup (VR-4)
before.description: The all-wheel-drive transfer case on early 3000GT VR-4 models can leak gear oil past its seals and O-rings, and because the unit holds very little fluid, even a slow leak starves the bearings. NHTSA issued two recalls for this defect (93V-033 and 02V-143) because bearing failure can lock the entire drivetrain without warning at highway speed, causing loss of vehicle control. Many cars never received the recall reseal, and 3si.org forum threads document failures decades later.
before.solution: Check whether recalls 93V033000 and 02V143 were performed (the 2002 remedy installed a reseal kit and replaced damaged cases). Otherwise, have the transfer case resealed at the first sign of leakage and inspect/top off the fluid regularly; a case showing bearing or gear damage must be replaced.
symptoms: Gear oil spots under the middle of the car
Burnt gear-oil smell after driving
Whining or growling from beneath the floor that rises with speed
Driveline binding or shudder in tight turns
Sudden grinding or lockup from the drivetrain

before.title: ECU Electrolytic Capacitor Leakage Causing Stalling and No-Start (1991-1993)
before.description: The electrolytic capacitors inside 1991-1993 ECUs leak corrosive electrolyte with age and heat cycling, eating copper traces off the circuit board. The result is erratic running, stalling, intermittent or complete no-start, and — if left long enough — an unrepairable ECU. The 3000GT/Stealth community considers preventive recapping mandatory on any unrepaired first-generation car; a telltale fishy 'rotten seafood' odor from the center console means electrolyte is already escaping.
before.solution: Remove the ECU and have the three electrolytic capacitors replaced (about $1 each in parts, or $100-300 at an electronics/ECU repair service), with board trace repair if electrolyte damage has started. Recap proactively before symptoms appear — a board with eaten traces may need a replacement ECU.
symptoms: Intermittent hard start or no-start
Engine stalling or sudden power loss while driving
Erratic idle and random driveability glitches
Fishy or rotten-seafood smell from the center console
Rapid clicking or chattering from under the dash

before.title: Front Brake Hose Cracking at Full Steering Lock (NHTSA Recall 96V-143)
before.description: On 1991-1994 cars, the front wheel-side brake hoses can crack when the steering is at full lock with the suspension at full travel, leaking brake fluid. NHTSA recall 96V143 covered roughly 10,000 vehicles built between August 1990 and November 1993 because the resulting fluid loss reduces braking effectiveness and increases crash risk. Original hoses on surviving cars are now over 30 years old, making cracking and weeping even more likely.
before.solution: Mitsubishi's recall remedy replaced both front wheel-side hoses with revised assemblies; verify recall completion by VIN. On any car still wearing original rubber hoses, replace all four brake hoses with new OEM or stainless-braided lines.
symptoms: Brake warning lamp illuminates
Brake fluid wetness on the inner front wheel or tire
Low or dropping brake fluid level
Soft or sinking brake pedal after hard turning maneuvers

before.title: Getrag AWD Manual Transmission Synchro Wear and Gear Grind (VR-4 5-Speed/6-Speed)
before.description: The Getrag-built AWD gearboxes in the VR-4 (W5MG1 5-speed through 1993, W6MG1 6-speed from 1994) are notorious for worn synchronizers, especially 1st-2nd and 2nd-3rd, causing grinding shifts. The synchros are undersized for the mass of the gears at high engine speed, so spirited driving wears them quickly; continuing to drive through the grind chews up gears and sliders, many of which are no longer available new. Rebuilds require specialist knowledge and parts kits from community vendors.
before.solution: Rebuild the transmission with updated synchro kits (R'venge Performance, Jack's Transmissions and similar specialists supply parts) at the first sign of regular grinding, before gear and slider damage compounds the bill. Use the correct fluid and double-clutch or slow shifts to extend synchro life in the meantime.
symptoms: Grinding on the 1-2 or 2-3 shift, especially at higher RPM
Notchy, baulky shifting when cold
Crunch when downshifting without rev-matching
Gradually worsening refusal to engage a gear quickly

before.title: Hydraulic Lash Adjuster 'Lifter Tick' on the 6G72 V6
before.description: The 6G72's hydraulic lash adjusters are prone to internal varnish buildup and wear, producing the platform's famous ticking noise at idle that rises with RPM. Dirty oil or extended change intervals make the adjusters bleed down and stick, increasing valvetrain clearance. It is mostly an annoyance, but a chronically loud, sticking adjuster accelerates rocker and cam lobe wear over time.
before.solution: Start with frequent oil changes and a cleaning additive regimen (community-proven options include a Rislone or Lucas treatment cycle, or pulling and cleaning the adjusters); persistent tick is cured by replacing the 24 lash adjusters, with upgraded 'big bore' Gen3 lifters or solid-lifter conversions sold specifically for this engine.
symptoms: Rhythmic ticking from the top of the engine at idle
Tick frequency increases with engine RPM
Noise is loudest at cold start and may fade when warm
Tick improves temporarily after an oil change

before.title: Pop-Up Headlight Motor and ETACS Failures (1991-1993)
before.description: Pre-facelift cars use motorized pop-up headlights controlled by the ETACS body module, and after 30+ years the motors, internal position switches, fuses, and ETACS relays commonly fail. Lights stick up, stick down, raise slowly, or only one side operates (the classic 'wink'). Because the motor always spins one direction and is stopped by a position switch inside the assembly, diagnosis confuses many owners — replacing a motor alone often does not fix it.
before.solution: Diagnose systematically: try the manual pop-up button (if it works there but not from the headlight switch, suspect the column switch; if neither works, test the fuse, motor, internal position switch, and ETACS unit). Used motors and ETACS repairs are the usual fix; a manual knob under the hood raises the lights as a roadside workaround.
symptoms: One or both headlights will not raise or retract
One headlight stuck up while the other works (the 'wink')
Slow, jerky, or grinding headlight movement
Lights respond to the manual dash button but not the headlight switch

before.title: Timing Belt and Hydraulic Tensioner Failure Destroying the Interference DOHC 6G72
before.description: The DOHC 24-valve 6G72 in the SL and VR-4 is an interference engine: if the timing belt snaps or the known-weak hydraulic tensioner bleeds down and lets the belt skip teeth, pistons strike open valves. Documented failures have bent as many as 17 of the engine's 24 valves, turning a missed $1,000 service into a $3,000-5,000 cylinder head job. Oil from leaking cam seals or valve covers contaminating the belt accelerates failure, and the cramped transverse V6 layout makes the 60,000-mile/5-year service frequently deferred.
before.solution: Replace the timing belt, hydraulic tensioner, idler pulleys, and water pump as a set every 60,000 miles or 5 years, fixing any cam/crank seal oil leaks at the same time. On a car with unknown service history, do the belt service before driving the car hard.
symptoms: Ticking, whirring, or slapping noise from the front timing cover
Engine cranks freely but will not start after a belt failure
Sudden rough running or misfires after the belt skips teeth
Oil seepage around the timing covers contaminating the belt
Unknown or overdue belt service history

before.title: VR-4 4WS Rear Steering Pump and Hard Line Leaks
before.description: The all-wheel-steering (4WS) system on the 1991-1996 VR-4 (and select 1991-1993 SL trims) uses a dedicated rear-mounted hydraulic pump driven off the rear-differential pinion. The pump's flanged metal feed line is mounted under the car and rusts heavily over time. When the line corrodes through or the pump seal fails, owners lose all 4WS fluid quickly, trigger the 4WS warning light, and can even lose front power steering assist because the system shares a fluid reservoir. Replacement is brutal because the bolted-on hard line is not sold separately - a full new rear pump assembly runs ~$900+ and parts can take 3 months to source.
before.solution: Inspect the flanged feed/return line at the rear pump for rust and weeping. For small low-pressure leaks, cut out the corroded section and bridge with high-pressure hose and double-clamped fittings as a temporary fix. For high-pressure-side or pump-internal leaks, the proper repair requires dropping the rear subframe to access the pump (parts ~$900 OEM, labor 6-10 hours). Many long-term VR-4 owners install a 4WS delete kit with block-off plates that bypasses the rear pump and hard-locks the rear steering rack, eliminating the failure point entirely ($150-$400 in parts).
symptoms: 4WS warning light illuminated on dashboard
Puddle of red/amber power steering fluid under rear of vehicle
Power steering reservoir empties repeatedly
Loss of front power steering assist (shared reservoir)
Whining noise from rear pump area
Visible rust or wet residue on the hard line at the back of the rear pump

proposal.title: VR-4 4WS Rear Steering Pump and Hard Line Leaks
proposal.description: The reviewed 3000GT corpus contains communication 52608 for a new power-steering hose on 1997 vehicles, outside the frozen 1991-1996 range. It does not establish recurring VR-4 rear-steering-pump seal failure, underbody hard-line corrosion, shared-reservoir loss of front assist, the frozen replacement cost or a universal 4WS-delete remedy. The frozen engine metadata also includes a naturally aspirated engine even though the title asserts VR-4 scope.
proposal.solution: Verify that the vehicle is equipped with four-wheel steering and identify the exact hydraulic layout. Clean the system and trace the highest fresh-fluid point while checking the reservoir, front and rear circuits, hard lines, flexible sections, fittings, rack and pump. Confirm whether a line is pressure or return side before specifying any repair. Do not buy hose, fittings, a rear pump, block-off plates or a delete kit from this page; the installed system, leak point, pressure duty and road-legal repair must be proven first.
symptoms: factory four-wheel-steering equipment verified
highest fresh-fluid source traced after cleaning
front/rear and pressure/return paths identified
affectedSystems: rear steering pump, lines and fittings
power-steering reservoir and front/rear assist paths
